written_proof_findings.finding: For d>=1, full matrix algebra excludes nonzero proper invariant subspaces. A nonzero d^2 minor persists under extension of scalars, proving absolute irreducibility. The rank-one alternative needs both cyclic spans; their outer products form a basis of the whole matrix space.

Minimal filtration containment of a simple submodule gives an isomorphism to one simple factor. Checking complete Hom spaces, not selected maps, captures every simple submodule; the proposed containing submodule must itself be semisimple.

Successive point stabilizers preserve each refined cell, so their orbit indices are bounded by the chosen cell sizes. Discreteness on the point set and distinct support subsets make the final stabilizer trivial. Complete minimum supports are invariant under all coordinate code automorphisms.

The full character proof works over every finite field: a nonzero F_q-linear functional from C is onto F_q. The additive-character orthogonality sum and coordinate factorization give the stated Krawtchouk coefficients. This is expressly classical, not a novelty claim.
RR^T=0 gives Q^2=0 and self-orthogonality of im Q; adjoining j also requires Rj=0 and j^Tj=0.

The counted candidate set is a subset of the code and invariant under the transitive group. Every true minimum can be moved into the bounded-message region; equality of finite counts there implies equality of all minimum sets.
